8.3.3.3 Water Quality
The Coley Creek Reservoir would impound the headwaters of Coley Creek and an unnamed tributary to Coley Creek. Water quality data are not available for these streams. However, Staff expects that the water in Coley Creek is of good quality, similar to other tributaries to Lake Jocassee. Impacts of construction and operation have been discussed earlier.
8.3.3.4 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
Flow and channel characteristics indicate the Coley Creek to be of the small headwater pool and riffle type of stream, surrounded by moderate to steep slopes that support moderate to dense vegetation, forming a symmetrical tight enclosure (Figure 8-6). No unique scenic or esthetic resources exist within the Coley Creek alternative that cannot be found in the proposed Bad Creek site and the other two alternative sites, as well as in any of the numerous adjacent valleys. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater esthetic attributes, the Coley Creek site has been rated 7, compared with a rating of 3, 7, and 5 given to the proposed Bad Creek site and the Bearcamp Creek and Long Spur Ridge sites, respectively (Dysart, et al., 1973).
Impacts on scenic and esthetic resources resulting from construction of this proposed alternative would drastically change the landscape, the degree of change depending on the size and character of project lands and appurtenant facilities.
8.3.3.5 Recreation
The Coley Creek alternative would inundate more of a combined land-water base of recreational opportunities than the proposed Bad Creek Project. The site, located in a remote and undeveloped part of the region adjacent to the Bearcamp Creek site, now provides opportunities for high-quality, low-density, primitive-type outdoor recreation. Present public use is limited by the lack of good accessibility and the absence of user facilities in the area. On a scale from 0 to 10, with higher number values representing greater recreational attributes, the Coley Creek site has been rated 7, compared with a rating of 4 for the Bad Creek site (Dysart, et al., 1973). The basis for the rating system in discussed in Section 8.3.1.5.
